warnings.message: Same full target sentence is reused across multiple scored activities.

manualReview.scope: Model/editor semantic and pedagogy review of Lesson 0079; not an independent human or real-learner test.

englishNaturalness.evidence: ‘The bus is at the end’ and ‘Wait at the end’ are plausible short location utterances in a route/waiting context.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: Persian copy consistently renders end as the endpoint of a route or place.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: One concrete bounded noun sense is practiced in two simple location frames.

distractorQuality.evidence: Distractors do not create a competing endpoint interpretation.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: A cafe waiting-line conversation can naturally involve identifying an endpoint and telling someone where to wait.

difficultyFit.evidence: The target remains within short A1 location language.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: The noun returns across listening, recognition, guided response and hidden retrieval.

transferQuality.evidence: The learner moves from describing a location to giving a waiting instruction.

overallCoherence.evidence: Scenario, target constructions and retrieval task align.

learnerExperience.evidence: No real learner test is claimed; confidence is limited to model/editor review.

limitations: No independent human or real learner test has been performed.
Only the bounded endpoint sense is reviewed.
Audio prosody is outside this text-stage review.
resolvedFindings: Target meaning is stable across both learner turns.
Persian translations preserve the intended endpoint sense.
The cafe arc returns after required spacing with learner-role rotation.
